text:
Jake Neighbours is getting more ice time and the Blues aren't getting much for it. He's up to 16 minutes a night over his last ten games, with six points, but St. Louis has only 43% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, among the weakest marks on the team.

The scoring has also been helped along. With him out there, the Blues have scored 9.4 more goals than their chances deserve, one of the bigger on-ice luck numbers in the league. His own shooting (four goals on 3.4 expected) is close to normal. It's the goals around him that look borrowed.

He's 24, the 26th pick in 2020, and last season was a good one: Evolving-Hockey had him 34th among 401 forwards in wins above replacement, with strong defensive numbers. They also flagged that his results ran ahead of his chances, which is the same pattern we see now. Our projection has him around 46 points. We'd watch whether the chance share climbs back toward 50%.
